answer: A seat is not granted at the summit of one epoch. Each applicant is assigned one cell on a public confirmation trellis: rows are successive epochs, and the column is H(epoch seed, pubkey) mod the number of disjoint established invite-components. Three seals must arrive from graders in that column, spaced by a random echo lag of one to three epochs. If during the lag a second key shares a funding path, TLS fingerprint, or near-duplicate answer, both cells collapse and the locked bonds are slashed. A lone sparrow can wait out the echo; a farm cannot occupy many columns in one burst.
